atomicity.reason: One obligation: the transfer function from highest cell temperature to the temperature-driven share. The 100 % plateau, the 0 % plateau and the linear interpolation are branches of one piecewise-linear definition and depend on each other (‘those two points’ is defined only by the other clauses), so dropping any clause leaves an incomplete function rather than a separate complete requirement; the ‘and’ joins cases of one function, not independent obligations.

comprehensibility.reason: No abbreviations and no forward references; the body names the subject, the input (highest cell temperature), the output (a percentage share of the permitted discharge power) and the complete transfer function, so it reads correctly on its own. ‘Temperature-driven share’ and ‘permitted discharge power’ are domain vocabulary used the same way by the parent and by SWREQ_SUSTAINED_LOAD_LIMIT. Wording nit, not scored down: upstream says ‘full permitted value’ / ‘full permitted discharge power’ while this body drops ‘full’.

feasibility.reason: Piecewise-linear arithmetic on one input is implementable with ordinary technology and nothing stated elsewhere contradicts it: the values match REQ_POWER_DERATING exactly, the ramp reaches 0 % at 60 °C just as REQ_CELL_OVERTEMPERATURE opens the contactors above 60 °C (so derating completes before the protective trip), and the minimum rule in SWREQ_LIMIT_MINIMUM and the ramp-versus-hysteresis split in DEC_HYSTERESIS_BANDS are compatible with it. The steep 20 %/K slope amplifies sensor error, but that is a system-accuracy matter outside this computation.

parent_fit.reason: ARCH_POWER_LIMIT_CALCULATOR says it ‘computes the temperature-driven limit as a linear ramp from 100 % at 55 °C to 0 % at 60 °C highest cell temperature’; this need specifies exactly that clause with identical values and the same driving quantity, and leaves the actuator-driven share, the sustained-load share and the minimum to SWREQ_LIMIT_MINIMUM and SWREQ_SUSTAINED_LOAD_LIMIT, so it covers a distinct part of the parent. It also carries the upstream REQ_POWER_DERATING obligation (full value at 55 °C, linearly to zero at 60 °C) without drift.

unambiguity.reason: The ramp itself has one reading, but its input is underspecified at the edges. The need says ‘highest cell temperature’ while the parent REQ_POWER_DERATING (ASIL B) says ‘highest valid cell temperature’, and SWREQ_TEMP_EXTREMA states that a cycle with no valid sample publishes no figures and reports the thermal picture as unavailable. The need defines the share only for a numeric temperature, so implementers could return 100 %, 0 % or hold the previous value in that case (and an invalid-flagged reading might or might not feed the ramp) and each would claim compliance; the downstream temperature_share_pct accepts only an int, so the case is not modelled there either. This does not change the core meaning, hence 1 rather than 0, and I fail closed because the function guards against overtemperature.
unambiguity.suggestion: Name the ramp input as the highest valid cell temperature published by the evaluator, and state what share applies in a cycle in which the evaluator publishes no figure (for example ‘the share is 0 %’, or ‘the previous share is held for N cycles, then 0 %’), or reference the swreq that owns that case.

verifiability.reason: Both thresholds, both output values, the units and the boundary inclusivity (‘at or below’, ‘at or above’) are stated, and ‘linear interpolation’ fixes the value everywhere in between (57.5 °C gives 50 %, 56 °C gives 80 %), so pass/fail needs no subjective reading: points below, on, inside and above the band tell a linear ramp from a step or a curve. No numeric tolerance or update cadence is given; I treated those as test-design details for deterministic arithmetic, not a missing success condition. The one case a test cannot be derived for (no valid temperature available) is scored once, under unambiguity.

summary: Crisp, single-obligation piecewise-linear ramp that matches ARCH_POWER_LIMIT_CALCULATOR and REQ_POWER_DERATING exactly and is directly testable, with one point deducted on unambiguity because it is silent on the invalid or unavailable temperature case that SWREQ_TEMP_EXTREMA can produce.
